title: Exceeding the Parametric Drive Strength Threshold in Nonlinear Circuits
summary: We demonstrate that a nonlinear coupler undergoes ionization under strong parametric driving, leading to a breakdown of coherent control. Through experiments and numerical simulations, we associate this behavior with drive-induced chaotic dynamics, characterized using the instantaneous Floquet spectrum.

title: Quantized Frequency-Domain Polarization of Driven Phases of Matter
summary: We study signatures of drive-induced phases on the Floquet lattice. The average position of Floquet eigenstates along the frequency axis can be written in terms of a non-adiabatic Berry phase, which we interpret as frequency-domain polarization. Whenever this polarization is quantized to a nontrivial value, the phase cannot be continuously connected to a time-independent state.

title: Robust Topological Invariants of Topological Crystalline Phases in the Presence of Impurities
summary: We show that robust basis-independent topological invariants can be generically constructed for topological crystalline phases using projected symmetry operators. The real-space topological markers are exponentially localized to the fixed points of the spatial symmetry, protecting them against impurities.

title: Local Imaging of Diamagnetism in Proximity-Coupled Niobium Nanoisland Arrays on Gold Thin Films
summary: We study the effect of engineered disorder on the local magnetic response of proximity-coupled superconducting island arrays by comparing scanning SQUID susceptibility measurements to a junction network model.

title: Computer-Aided Quantization and Numerical Analysis of Superconducting Circuits
summary: We present work utilizing symbolic computer algebra and numerical diagonalization routines versatile enough to tackle a variety of superconducting circuits. Results are accessible through a newly released module of the scqubits package.

title: Fate of Quantum Many-Body Scars in the Presence of Disorder
summary: We study the stability of quantum many-body scars against disorder in the PXP model of Rydberg atoms. Scarred eigenstates persist at weak disorder but are eventually destroyed at strong disorder.

title: Imaging and Controlling Vortex Dynamics in Mesoscopic Superconductor–Normal-Metal–Superconductor Arrays
summary: We use a scanning probe technique to study vortex dynamics in superconducting systems by leveraging the resonant behavior of a magnetic-tipped cantilever, obtaining spatial patterns that encode the vortex energy landscape.

title: Dissipative Vortex Dynamics in Superconducting Arrays
summary: We perform current-voltage measurements on low resistance superconductor-normal-superconductor arrays in finite magnetic fields, finding that the behavior can be explained by a history-dependent dissipative force.

title: Many-Body Mobility Edge due to Symmetry-Constrained Dynamics and Strong Interactions
summary: We provide numerical evidence combined with an analytical understanding of the many-body mobility edge for the strongly anisotropic spin-1/2 XXZ model in a random magnetic field.

title: Entanglement of a 3D Generalization of the Kitaev Model on the Diamond Lattice
summary: We study the entanglement properties of a three-dimensional generalization of the Kitaev honeycomb model on the diamond lattice, characterizing topological and gapless phases using entanglement entropy and the entanglement spectrum.

title: Signatures of Metal-Insulator and Topological Phase Transitions in the Entanglement of One-Dimensional Disordered Fermions
summary: We study one-dimensional disordered fermions undergoing metal-insulator or topological phase transitions, developing entanglement tools that reveal metallic states and show clear signatures of localization transitions even with interactions.

title: Topological Criticality in the Chiral-Symmetric AIII Class at Strong Disorder
summary: We derive a covariant real-space formula for the winding number and show it remains quantized even when the bulk spectrum is completely localized. An abrupt change to a trivial value marks a critical point where the localization length diverges.

title: Characterizing Disordered Fermion Systems Using the Momentum-Space Entanglement Spectrum
summary: We propose the momentum-space entanglement spectrum as a means of characterizing disordered models, showing that localization in one dimension can be characterized by the momentum space entanglement between left and right movers.

title: Unconventional Bose-Einstein Condensations from Spin-Orbit Coupling
summary: We find that multi-component bosons with spin-orbit coupling provide an unconventional type of BEC where the condensate spontaneously generates a half-quantum vortex combined with skyrmion-type spin texture, breaking time-reversal symmetry.

title: Efficient Calculation of Coulomb Matrix Elements for Bilayers of Confined Charge Carriers with Arbitrary Spatial Separation
Coulomb Correlations of a Few Body System of Spatially Separated Charges
summary: Hartree-Fock and Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov study of a few body system of spatially separated charge carriers. We compute the correlation energy and discuss how it can determine the formation of indirect excitons relevant to Bose-Einstein condensation.
